identity.courage_tooltip:
They represent your ability to do what you want.
Whenever you need to do something that could go wrong—running, jumping, hiding, distracting, fleeing, attacking, etc.—you must use your Courage.
identity.health_tooltip:
They represent your vitality.
Whenever you find yourself in a hostile environment or facing a dangerous creature, your Soul Points will be at risk. If they reach zero, your Protector dies.
identity.honor_tooltip:
The air, waterways, creatures, and shadows perceive Honor around you. The greater your Honor, the more you are respected.
By helping others, protecting your memories, and accomplishing your mission, you will gain Honor. But beware: giving in to violence or harming a creature will cause you to lose Honor. Honor Points can be negative, and if so, your freedom to buy items or enter certain places will be limited.
identity.inspiration_tooltip:
This is your connection to the world around you.
Whenever you show creativity, help someone, or are happy with a discovery you’ve made, you can reward yourself by gaining an Inspiration Point. Be kind to yourself whenever you contribute to shaping the world around you.
identity.money_tooltip: They allow you to trade, buying or selling items.
identity.stamina_tooltip:
They represent your ability to keep going.
Your Stamina Points determine how many items you can carry or how fast the Clock advances.
identity.title: Identity & Stats

floodedPlains.1: **The water surrounding your legs seems to heal your fatigue and encourages you to travel.** You gain a +1 Courage bonus (maximum: 5) until you cross the boundary between day and night on the Clock.
floodedPlains.2: **A traveler crosses your path.** Go to page 57 and define who you have met. *If you return here, the traveler will no longer be there.*
floodedPlains.3|4:
**You discover a Trading Post.**
*To learn more, refer to page 23.*
floodedPlains.5:
**You encounter a Hedgehog.** To learn more about these creatures, read page 22. **Draw a card** to find out what type of Hedgehog you have found.
- ♥♦ A **peaceful** Hedgehog.
- ♠♣ An **aggressive** Hedgehog.
floodedPlains.6: **You encounter a celestial goose,** which can be ridden when fed or if you succeed in a Courage test. It can take you to any already explored cell without advancing your Clock. Afterwards, it leaves you to return to the Flooded Plains.

mushroomJungle.1: **You are caught in a spore storm.** No protective equipment can save you in this situation. **Lose 1 point in the attribute of your choice.**
mushroomJungle.2: **A Ruin appears in the middle of the mass of mushrooms that stretches in all directions.** *Consult page 63 if you want to enter.*
mushroomJungle.3|4: **You discover a group of Mousserons.** To determine their number, roll 1D6. *To learn more about Mousserons, refer to page 27.*
mushroomJungle.5:
**You discover a Titan Boletus,** a giant mushroom. Draw a card to determine what type it is.
*To learn more about Titan Boletus, refer to page 26.*
- ♦ A **stationary** Titan Boletus.
- ♥ An **ambulant** Titan Boletus.
- ♣ A **stationary and venomous** Titan Boletus.
- ♠ An **ambulant and venomous** Titan Boletus.
mushroomJungle.6: **You discover a Titan Boletus lying on the ground.** It has perished or forgotten to wake up, thus giving life to thousands of other mushrooms. *Go to page 26 and choose an item from the collection table even if you don’t have climbing equipment.*

fieldSea.1:
**Strong headwinds make your journey laborious.** Eat or succeed in a Courage test to resist them. If you fail, lose 1 point of Endurance or an item of your choice.
*The next time you pass through this place, these violent winds will have ceased.*
fieldSea.2: **A traveler crosses your path.** Go to page 57 and [define](/en/generators/npc) who you have met. *If you return here, the traveler will no longer be there.*
fieldSea.3: **You discover a small community garden!** Go to the *collection table* (page 30) and choose an item of your choice without needing the appropriate tool. Mark this garden as **harvested**. You must **water** the garden to be able to reuse it another day.
fieldSea.4|5:
**You arrive at a Cucurbitus farm.**
*To learn more about Cucurbitus, refer to page 30.*
When you find a Cucurbitus farm, go to page 42 and **draw 5 cards** to define what it looks like.
fieldSea.6:
**You encounter a creature.** Draw a card from the deck to find out what creature you have found.
- ♦ A **red** Sauriflore (see page 30).
- ♥ A **yellow** Sauriflore (see page 30).
- ♣ A **white** Sauriflore (see page 30).
- ♠ A Pizi (see page 62).

shadowForest.1:
**Dense and ancestral shadows tightly embrace you.** Due to the darkness, everything you have found in these three cells of the Shadow Forest is erased from your journal and map.
*If you pass through this cell again, draw other encounters.*
shadowForest.2|3: **You arrive in a [Bruja village](/en/generators/village?f=bruja).** To learn more about Brujas, see page 18. When you find a Bruja village, go to page 43 and **draw 5 cards** to define the place.
shadowForest.4: **You find a Swarm of fireflies.** Once a day, if you pass through this place, you can recover 1 point in any Attribute.
shadowForest.5|6:
**You encounter a creature.** Draw a card to find out which one:
- ♦ A group of **Yabas** (see page 19).
- ♥ A **lost Yaba** (see page 19).
- ♣ A **Warrior Tree**, which triggers a combat (see page 19).
- ♠ A **Pizi** (see page 62).

silentDesert.1:
**A Ruin emerges from the sandy rocks.**
*Go to page 63 if you want to explore it.*
silentDesert.2:
**You discover an oasis.** *To learn more, refer to page 36.* Draw a card to find out what type of oasis you have found.
- ♥♦ A **palm paradise**.
- ♠♣ A **cactus sanctuary**.
silentDesert.3|4:
**You encounter a Kiore.** *To learn more, consult page 34. Go to page 57 if you want to define the Kiore's personality.
If you return here, the Kiore will no longer be there.*
silentDesert.5|6:
**You encounter a Desert Scarab.** *To learn more, read page 37.* Draw a card to discover what type of Scarab you have encountered.
- ♦ A **peaceful** Scarab.
- ♥ An **aggressive** Scarab.
- ♠♣ A **flipped** Scarab.

giganticGardens.1:
**You face a swarm of giant bees.** They rush towards you to attack, and you must either fight or flee.
*The next time you pass through this cell, this event repeats.*
giganticGardens.2|3:
**You discover a garden of normal-sized Lareons.** *To learn more, see page 41.* Draw a card to discover the type of flowers that grow in this garden.
- ♥♦ **Red** Lareons.
- ♠♣ **Yellow** Lareons.
giganticGardens.4:
**You discover a field of golden petals.** Draw a card from the deck to discover what type of flowers you have found.
*In both cases, nothing will grow here again after your passage.*
- ♥♦ Golden petals — can be harvested and sold for 100 coins.
- ♠♣ Golden shoots — can be harvested as 1D6 food.
giganticGardens.5:
**You encounter a luxurious whale.** *To learn more, read page 40.* Draw a card to find out what type of whale you have encountered.
- ♥♦ A **peaceful** luxurious whale.
- ♠♣ An **aggressive** luxurious whale.
giganticGardens.6: **You discover a pile of giant bones,** those of a luxurious whale. See the *collection table* on page 40 to determine what you find there.

shadowForest.hint: For collecting resources in the Shadow Forest, you can use an Axe. To use it, remove 1 durability point from it, then choose the item of your choice from the gathering table above. Otherwise, successfully pass a Courage Test to do without the necessary equipment.

mushroomJungle.warn: Gathering in the Mushroom Jungle requires finding and reaching the top of a Titan Boletus (see page 26).

fieldSea.hint: For collecting resources in the Field Sea, you can use Gardening Shears. To use them, remove 1 durability point from them, then choose the item of your choice from the gathering table above. Otherwise, successfully pass a Courage Test to do without the necessary equipment.

silentDesert.hint: For collecting resources in the Silent Desert, you can use a Pickaxe. To use it, remove 1 durability point from it, then choose the item of your choice from the gathering table above. Otherwise, successfully pass a Courage Test to do without the necessary equipment.

giganticGardens.warn: Gathering in the Gigantic Gardens requires finding and reaching the garden on the back of a luxurious whale (see page 40).

faq.answer_1:
ProMe, for “**Pro**tector” and “**Me**mories” is a companion ~app~ website for “[The Protector’s Memories](https://www.criticalkit.co.uk/products/the-protectors-memories)”, a solo RPG by Enzo Salviato. It is suggested to have the app open while playing the game, as a reference and to track your progress. It is mainly for playing the game digitally (though not entirely, as using the official manual is required).

The game is exceptional, but requires taking notes on paper; something that is personally tedious for me. That’s why I developed this digital version, to shift the note-taking and annotation of the map onto the computer (or mobile).
faq.answer_2: The mapping module uses modern CSS features that are not yet well supported by all browsers. That’s why it’s best to use the Chrome browser, as it’s the one I use for development. As for why I didn’t extend support to other browsers: creating a hexagonal grid is complicated; I had to choose between using modern tech to keep things simple, or developing the entire map system with HTML Canvas, which I didn’t want to do.
faq.answer_3:
Encounters are not implemented, so each move requires rolling a die (physically or via the app) and referring to the rulebook to determine which encounter occurs.
In addition, the stock of shops is not implemented either. This means that when creating a village, it is necessary to define the offers manually, then note them in the journal to return to them later.
faq.answer_4: For better or for worse, the game doesn’t have any concept of gender, so all characters — playable or not — are genderless. I thought it would be interesting and more immersive to have the ability to define the gender of the characters. It’s completely optional, and it’s permissive on purpose with multiple options.

context_by_rank.2: **{name} is looking for something.** Maybe something not sold in this village, or something only found far from here? But beyond that, {gender, select, man {he} woman {she} other {they}} seems afraid of the unknown. Maybe there’s a story behind it.
context_by_rank.3: **{name} dreams of traveling to another village.** Maybe you could accompany them and learn more about their motivations and desires!
context_by_rank.4: **{name} is very ill and doesn’t have much time left.** {gender, select, man {He} woman {She} other {They}} is {gender, select, man {alone} woman {alone} other {alone}} and no one to support them in these difficult moments. Maybe a conversation would bring some comfort? *Next time you visit this place, you’ll need to succeed a Courage test to find {gender, select, man {him} woman {her} other {them}}.*
context_by_rank.5: **{name} is seeking friendship—or maybe love?** You’re not sure, but {gender, select, man {he} woman {she} other {they}} seems to feel {gender, select, man {lonely} woman {lonely} other {lonely}}. You can help them find someone who seeks something similar.
context_by_rank.6: **{name} longs for a loved one.** Maybe it’s someone who lives elsewhere or has just left. But {gender, select, man {he} woman {she} other {they}} is also looking for a very special object that reminds them of this person. What is this object?
context_by_rank.7: {name} is a **cartographer**. You meet {gender, select, man {him} woman {her} other {them}} as {gender, select, man {he} woman {she} other {they}} is about to leave the village and recognizes you as a traveler. {gender, select, man {He} woman {She} other {They}} offers you one of their maps. Roll a D6: *Location Map (1-3)* or *Biome Map (4-6)* (see page 49).
context_by_rank.8: {name} is **painting a picture**. Realizing you’re a traveler, {gender, select, man {he} woman {she} other {they}} asks if you have a sketch of an unknown place, or if you can describe a panorama you’ve seen on your travels! {gender, select, man {He} woman {She} other {They}} has never ventured far from their village and is seeking inspiration!
context_by_rank.9: There are rumors of mysterious Ruins scattered across the world, and **{name} is curious to learn more**. Seeing you’re a traveler, {gender, select, man {he} woman {she} other {they}} approaches you to see if you have any information to share!
context_by_rank.10: **{name} speaks a name while wandering the village.** Who is it? Why are they saying this name? What happened? *If you need to create a name, consult the table on page 60.*
context_by_rank.A: **{name} is mourning a recent loss.** {gender, select, man {He} woman {She} other {They}} may have lost a pet or a close friend. Maybe a conversation would be welcome? Or perhaps {gender, select, man {he} woman {she} other {they}} just needs someone to listen?
context_by_rank.J: **{name} buys objects from other parts of the world and offers 100 coins for each item of interest.** Talk to them! Maybe you have something {gender, select, man {he} woman {she} other {they}} would like to acquire.
context_by_rank.Q: **{name} looks like someone you’ve met before.** Is it just an impression? You can always ask to be sure. {gender, select, man {He} woman {She} other {They}} may have crossed your path before, or maybe it’s a stranger with new stories to tell!
context_by_rank.K: **{name} is a builder.** {gender, select, man {He} woman {She} other {They}} tells you that with 3 wood and 3 iron, or 1,000 coins, {gender, select, man {he} woman {she} other {they}} can build the establishment of your choice in the village.

J.red: **City.** It is a **large colony**. Draw **3 additional establishment cards**; if you draw a **face card** (Jack, Queen, King), **ignore it** and draw again until you get a **numbered card**.
J.black: **Wonder.** The village is **exceptionally beautiful**. Describe it. You gain **2 Inspiration Points**.

Q.red: **Fortified.** The village is **surrounded by walls** with a **guarded entrance**. You must have **at least 1 Honor Point** to enter.
Q.black: **Lush.** It features a **body of water** (river, lake, etc.) and a **garden**. You can use the **biome collection table** **without special equipment**.

K.red: **Abandoned.** The buildings seem **uninhabited**. The **establishments are inoperable** until someone decides to **rebuild the village**.
K.black: **Nomadic.** The village **moves**. When you return to this **map cell**, you must succeed a **Courage test**. On **failure**, the village **is no longer there**.
